title: Topology-aware KV-tiling continuous batcher for mixed-length streams
creator: Alex Kim
description:
Background: Continuous batching performs well for homogeneous sequence lengths but we see persistent GPU memory fragmentation and tail latency increases when request mixes contain many short prompts interleaved with long responses. Current KV residency and slab allocation are conservative and cause underutilized GPU memory and frequent kv-evictions during long-turn spikes.

Scope: Implement a topology-aware KV-tiling policy in the continuous batcher that (a) partitions KV residency into per-cohort tiles by length/turn profile, (b) uses a lightweight reservoir admission controller to pin tiles temporarily during long-response phases, and (c) coordinates with the slot allocator to bias packing so that mixed-length cohorts co-reside in a cache-friendly layout. The change must preserve latency SLOs for P0 routes and reduce average token cost by lowering unnecessary evictions and GPU slab churn.

Non-goals: This ticket does not refactor the kernel-selection layer or change quantization heuristics. It also does not modify the API surface or customer-facing behavior beyond performance improvements.

Constraints: Must operate within the existing continuous-batcher runtime with minimal changes to the fast path (<=1 additional branch on hot path). Must be rollback-safe with a feature flag and have telemetry for tile occupancy, eviction rates, and failed pin attempts.
acceptance_criteria: Feature gated and rollout-able via runtime-1.20 feature-flag
End-to-end tests demonstrating 10-20% reduction in KV-eviction rate on mixed synthetic workload
No more than 5% median latency increase on P0 short-turn traffic in canary cluster
Decrease in GPU slab re-compaction events by 15% under mixed-length trace from production replay
Dashboard panels for tile occupancy, per-cohort eviction rate, pin-failure rate, and rollback metrics added to Console runtime-1.20
work_items: Design tiling scheme and mapping rules (length buckets + turn-profile hash)
Implement tile metadata in KV store and lightweight pin/unpin primitives
Add reservoir admission controller and heuristics for soft-pinning during long responses
Modify continuous-batcher slot allocator to prefer co-locating complementary cohorts
Add unit tests for tile allocation and pin logic
Integration test with GPU slab simulator and synthetic mixed-length traces
PR with rollout flag, migration guard, and feature toggle
Instrumentation: add telemetry and Console dashboard panels
Canary rollout plan and rollback playbook
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting — scoped tiling approach. Decided on 4 length buckets (<=32,33-128,129-512,>512) + turn-profile hashing for affinity.
2026-02-18: Prototype added pin/unpin API in local dev runtime. Microbench indicates ~0.4% additional CPU on hot path with branch elision.
2026-02-22: Integrated reservoir admission controller; initial heuristics use recent token-rate and per-slot age to prefer pins for long-turns.
2026-02-26: Integration tests with synthetic mixed stream show 12% reduction in eviction rate but a 3% median latency increase on short-turns in unoptimized packing.
2026-03-01: Slot allocator packing bias implemented; re-run tests show eviction reduction 18% and short-turn median latency delta within 1.2%. Preparing PR for review.
comments: Samir Patel (2026-02-14): Consider adding a backpressure signal from the KV store to slow admission during sustained high eviction bursts — could be a follow-up if pinning alone isn't enough.
Mateo Ruiz (2026-02-20): Prototype telemetry keys look good. Make sure tile IDs are stable across restarts to avoid metric churn.
Elena Novik (PM) (2026-02-25): Prioritize canary watches for customer routes that are latency-sensitive. Add explicit rollback criteria for token-cost regressions.
Code review note (Priya N.) (2026-03-01): Inline comments on reservoir parameters and a suggestion to make bucket boundaries configurable via runtime config. Will address in follow-up commit.
